newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar turns lower as volume picks up.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar turns lower as volume picks up.

text.p: Volume picked up on London's white sugar futures market on Friday afternoon with the open of New York trading and values took another swing to the downside.
Traders noted commission house selling of the nearby positions which was offset by scale-down buying by trade players, with the volume mainly compsed of outright deals.
Some buying of the white premium was also seen and a limited amount of switch trades.

"It's all pretty orderly and it's set into the Friday mode," said one trader. During the early part of the session London volume was static at a paltry 16 lots and the spot December contract managed to hold above nearby support at $321.50 per tonne.
At 1529 GMT December was 80 cents lower at $322.40 and March down $2.20 at $318.40. Volume amounted to 1,048 lots.
Traders said there was a singular lack of fresh fundamental news to spur sentiment on the whites, but cited earlier market talk of Russian demand for as much as 100,000 tonnes.
But London brokers discounted the talk that Russia was either open to buy or had bought already, saying it was too early in the season for purchases.

Belarus plans to buy 200,000 tonnes of raw sugar from Cuba and Latin America and has imposed a 35 percent value-added tax on refined sugar imports. A contract has also been signed for 120,000 tonnes of raws from South Africa.
Paris values also lost ground but volume stayed thin at 391 lots. December was down 40 cents at $322.50 and March was down $2.20 at $318.50.
